extracted.intended_audience: mathematics education researchers and undergraduate mathematics instructors (those designing proofs and assessment in undergraduate math)
extracted.subtask_description: Research and practical guidance on (1) what features mathematicians value in proofs presented to undergraduates and (2) implementing criterion-referenced assessment (CRA) in an undergraduate differential equations course. Targets design of proofs for pedagogy and construction/communication of assessment criteria and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make proof frameworks explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs for undergraduates should make the proof frameworks explicit (e.g., add introductory sentences or roadmaps that remind students of the meaning of definitions and outline how the proof will proceed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding introductory sentences can remind students of definitions and provide a roadmap; some participants found concluding sentences unnecessary. Making the framework explicit supports pedagogical clarity even if some experienced readers find the change verbose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and space important equations to highlight importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Format important equations so they are highlighted and not buried; spacing and visual appearance are important aspects that make proofs less condensed and easier to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper formatting can illustrate main ideas and reduce density; many participants preferred formatting because it made the proof easier to read and understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary calculations and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs should avoid adding unnecessary calculations or assumptions that do not contribute to the main idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnecessary steps or assumptions may distract the reader from the main ideas and encourage attempts to understand why they were included, thereby reducing pedagogical quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stating obvious assumptions that distract
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not state assumptions or add phrases that are obvious in context (e.g., explicitly saying 'f was real-valued' when it's implicit), since such statements can distract and divert attention from salient hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider what the intended audience already assumes; adding obvious information can be seen as adding words with no benefit and may confuse or distract students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add extra justification judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding an extra justification to bridge logical gaps is sometimes valued (it can help students with challenging inferences) but may be seen by others as diminishing pedagogical quality if the inference is obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is disagreement among mathematicians about the optimal level of detail. Include justifications where students are likely to struggle, but avoid over-explaining trivial steps; consider the audience's expected knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider audience when choosing level of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians do not agree on what would be obvious to a student, so the appropriate level of detail in a proof depends on the intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising proofs for pedagogical use, explicitly consider student background; disagreements among instructors imply making assumptions about student knowledge should be explicit or tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion-referenced assessment (CRA) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: CRA is assessment constructed to measure student performance with reference to clearly delineated learning tasks and predetermined goals/criteria, and fundamentally involves assessing a student without reference to the performance of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing CRA requires (1) an underlying set of course learning outcomes, (2) an assessment program designed to gather information about performance relative to those outcomes, and (3) communication of criteria and standards (a two-dimensional view) to inform students and assessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and state course learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly list the course learning outcomes that CRA will measure (examples provided: engage critical thinking and theoretical knowledge; identify/solve problems; communicate appropriately; demonstrate independence in retrieving/evaluating information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning outcomes serve as the anchors for criteria; assessment subtasks should be explicitly linked to these outcomes to make assessment informative and educational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct assessment program aligned to learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Design an assessment program to obtain information about student performance in relation to the stated learning outcomes (e.g., mix of assignments, exams, quizzes where some items are assessed using CRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain assessment integrity while mapping task subtasks to outcomes; for maximum transfer, use representative course tasks and map marks to outcome-related criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate criteria and standards clearly and early
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide students with the CRA criteria and the definitions of standards early in the semester and alongside assessment tasks so they understand how they will be judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students in the study reported criteria were made clear early and were easy to understand; however, instructors must also explain why criteria are provided and how students should use them to guide learning and interpret feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map marks to criteria (provide annotated criteria maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly map traditional marks/points to criteria related to learning outcomes (e.g., show how ticks/crosses translate into criterion-level percentages and grade descriptors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both traditional point-based annotations and an annotated criteria map helps students see not only where they lost points but which learning outcomes/subskills they need to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency-based standard allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of determining standards by weighting marks achieved in each criterion category and mapping the resulting percentage to grade levels (example: compute percent for criterion across item and translate to grade 6/7 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency of correct steps across criterion-related subtasks to allocate standards; authors note taxonomy of standard allocations is nontrivial and under further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use criterion categories (e.g., communication, problem solving)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group traditional right/wrong judgments into categories related to course learning outcomes such as communication and problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories provide a higher-level view of student strengths and weaknesses beyond a raw point total and must be clearly defined so students and graders understand them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully design and word criteria and standards to reflect graders' judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and standards must be constructed and worded so they match the kinds of judgments graders actually use when assessing student work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic staff should be closely guided in developing criteria; poor wording undermines the transparency and usefulness of CRA because students gather information about grading from these statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide both point-based feedback and higher-level criterion feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize feedback, present both traditional annotated solutions with points/ticks/crosses and an annotated criteria map that links those annotations to criterion-level performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dual feedback helps students interpret marks at a higher level (where they are progressing well and where they struggle) and supports learning more than points alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate students on how to use feedback; CRA alone is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating assessment criteria is not sufficient by itself to influence students' approaches; students must be taught how to use the feedback to guide learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found students understood and found CRA useful for understanding grading, but it did not change how they approached assessment tasks; instructors should explicitly instruct students on using feedback to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRA should not use normative (relative) comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: CRA involves assessing a student without reference to the performance of others; standards are absolute rather than norm-referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain absolute criteria/standards so grades reflect achievement relative to predetermined outcomes, not to cohort performance.
